title: Closed fibres are empty or singleton under point separation
statement: Let $k$ be an algebraically closed field [def-weil-algebraic-closure], let $X$ be a scheme locally of finite type over $k$ [def-weil-finite-type-morphism], let $Y$ be a scheme over $k$, and let $f:X\to Y$ be a morphism [def-weil-pbc-scheme-conventions]. Assume that distinct closed points of $X$ have distinct images under $f$. For every closed point $p\in Y$ [def-weil-closed-points], the fibre $f^{-1}(p)$ is either empty or the singleton set $\{x\}$ for one closed point $x\in X$.

source.place: Tag 0E8S, lemma-separate-points-tangent-vectors, proof after condition (1), with Tag 0478 for closed points in closures

proof.text: Fix a closed point $p\in Y$ and write $F=f^{-1}(\{p\})$. The singleton $\{p\}$ is closed, so $F$ is closed because morphisms of schemes are continuous. If $F$ is nonempty, choose $z\in F$. If $z$ were not closed, then [lem-sc-finite-type-nonclosed-closure-closed-points] would give infinitely many closed points in $\overline{\{z\}}$; since $F$ is closed and contains $z$, this closure lies in $F$, and all those closed points have image $p$, contradicting the assumed distinction of images of closed points. Thus every nonempty fibre contains a closed point.

source.place: Tag 0E8S, lemma-separate-points-tangent-vectors, proof after condition (1), using Tag 0478 for closed points in closures

proof.text: Every point $y\in F$ is closed by the same argument: if it were nonclosed, its closure would supply infinitely many closed points of $F$, all mapping to $p$. Since any two closed points of $F$ have the same image $p$, the hypothesis that distinct closed points have distinct images implies that there is at most one such point. Combined with step 1, $F$ is empty or $\{x\}$ for one closed point $x\in X$.
